answer: Before an agent’s vote counts, it must lock a stake and present a scarce, one-per-person credential. Random audits check for duplicate credentials; if an agent is proven to have reused one, its stake is slashed. A falcon-like watcher can flag suspicious clusters for review, while glacier-slow trust accrues to agents with clean histories. To multiply votes, an attacker must obtain more credentials and lock more capital, risking each stake if caught; a grove of aliases is no longer cheap influence.
